solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Area of London in which Unionist's lost

indicators.note: the clue says the Unionist is lost from the word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: in, as in fashionable, means popular
U is the standard abbreviation for Unionist; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A political observation about a London district where the Unionist candidate was defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' looks like a link but 'in' is the piece: IN = POPULAR, and 'lost' removes U.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district in the East End of London, in the borough of Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: D Arth shows this game old character!

definitions.text: D Arth shows this game old character

parts.words: D Arth shows this game old character
parts.note: DARTH with a gap put into it gives D ARTH; doing the same to the second name of the old film villain gives a gap in VADER

explanation.surface: A quirky caption pointing at the split name of the Star Wars villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Darth Vader is the 'old character': D ARTH shows a space in Darth, so the clue is pointing at a space in Vader, which is also the name of a classic arcade game.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic 1978 arcade shoot-'em-up, where players fire at ranks of descending aliens.

clue.text: Group's damned lies about fish getting caught

indicators.note: the statistics are wrapped about the fish and the catch, putting them inside

parts.note: from the saying 'lies, damned lies and statistics', so STATS
a ray is a flat fish
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone telling tall tales about a fish they supposedly landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damned lies' leans on the saying 'lies, damned lies and statistics' to give STATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stray Cats were an American rockabilly band of the early 1980s, a musical group.

clue.text: Reluctant to present some poetry

parts.note: some, as in a certain one, gives the article A
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who is shy about reciting a few lines of poetry in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disinclined or unwilling to do something is a synonym of reluctance.

clue.text: Movie star's reduced stature forever encapsulated by Berlioz et al in composition

indicators.note: the height and the forever go inside the rearranged composer letters, as in a capsule
a composition is a putting-together, so the letters of Berlioz et al are reassembled
reduced to its abbreviation, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: stature is height
AY (also AYE) is an old word meaning always, ever

explanation.surface: A film actor's small height captured forever in a musical work by Berlioz and others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movie star' is a woman, though 'stature' tempts toward a short actor. 'in composition' shuffles the composer and colleagues; 'encapsulated by' sets the short height and the forever inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood actress of Cleopatra and Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? was a major film star.

clue.text: Hacker infiltrating menu that children read

indicators.note: the bird has slipped in among the clue words, sitting inside a run of them

explanation.surface: A computer hacker breaking into the menu of a children's reading app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacker' suggests computers, but it is a bird that hacks at nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird wedges nuts in bark and hacks them open with its bill, hence a hacker.

clue.text: Take a long time over engagement ring?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned up and over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone dithering for ages before buying an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement ring' is not about marriage: it is the ring where fighters engage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or circular enclosure where combatants engage is a ring for fighting.

clue.text: Receiver makes lawman get to the point

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West lawman
to hone is to sharpen, bring to a point

explanation.surface: An instruction for a sheriff on how to talk to someone receiving a message: be concise.
explanation.definitionFit: A headphone or telephone piece held at the ear receives sound, so it is a receiver.

clue.text: Charge for butter

definitions.meaning: a butter here is one that butts, as a horned animal does

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's question about what dairy fat costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge at someone is to rush at them; the horned farm animal is famous for butting.

clue.text: Hypothetical cipher running through popular article on line

indicators.note: the cipher runs through the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
the is the definite article
RY, railway, is a line
a cipher is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Speculation about a secret code spreading through a popular newspaper piece on a phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only in principle, not tested in practice, is merely hypothetical.

clue.text: Island tour-guide, single one finding lost loves earlier

indicators.note: the other pieces come earlier, placed before the street guide

parts.note: single means one, the article A

indicators.note: the two loves are lost from the word, so those letters drop out

parts.note: one who finds something is a locator
love in tennis scores is zero, the letter O; two loves are OO
an A-Z is the London street atlas, a guide for touring the city

explanation.surface: A guide on a prison-island tour, alone, discovering lost lovers from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the British street-map book, a guide to touring a city. 'lost' drops the two tennis zeros from the finder, and 'earlier' puts the rest before the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The former prison stands on a rocky island in San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Brave Dad's getting over pain

indicators.note: in an across clue, getting over means placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is dad; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A father bravely recovering from an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun here: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Apache are one such people.

clue.text: Two members of our Kingdom joining sports club

parts.note: an insect and a flying mammal are two members of the animal kingdom, to which we belong
an insect and a flying mammal are two members of the animal kingdom, to which we belong

explanation.surface: Two people from Britain joining a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our Kingdom' suggests the UK but means the animal kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow bat is a club used in sport to hit the ball.

clue.text: One won't change with this preparation of meat for stew?

definitions.meaning: one raised to the third power is still one
cutting meat into small dice for a stew

explanation.surface: A cook claiming one never varies this method of preparing stewing meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a number to its third power leaves one unchanged; cutting meat into dice is the culinary sense.

clue.text: A writer or two following match?

parts.note: two words that follow match in tennis phrases: match ball and match point
two words that follow match in tennis phrases: match ball and match point

explanation.surface: A sports journalist or two covering the game afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is a pen, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a tiny rolling sphere at its tip is something that writes.

clue.text: Change starter in midday meal for quite a few gallons

indicators.note: the first letter of the meal word is changed for another

parts.note: luncheon is a formal midday meal

explanation.surface: Swapping the first course at lunch for a lot of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces L; only the definition settles it as P.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask holding roughly 70 to 120 gallons, so a lot of liquid.

clue.text: Lukewarm score?

parts.note: lukewarm water is neither cold nor hot, so not C and not H, on taps; a score is a cut

explanation.surface: A tepid result in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: On taps C is cold and H hot; lukewarm is neither, so NOT CH. A score is also a cut mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A score, in the sense of a small cut or nick, is a mark like this.

clue.text: Follower of Siegfried Sassoon, at last I am in the country, taking a breather

indicators.note: only the final letter of the poet's name is wanted

parts.note: in rustic dialect, 'I am' is 'I be'
a lung is what we breathe with

explanation.surface: A follower of the war poet Siegfried Sassoon resting in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siegfried Sassoon' reads as the poet, but Siegfried is the Wagner hero and Sassoon gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wagner's Ring cycle the dwarf race whose hoard Siegfried wins, and his own line, are associated with him.

clue.text: Breakfast (cooked) impulsive VIP binned

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form
the letters of VIP are thrown away from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A rash celebrity throwing out their cooked breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges IMPULSIVE once the letters of VIP are 'binned', leaving MULSIE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss cereal mix of oats, nuts and fruit is a common morning meal.

clue.text: Thus diminutive female indicated she's all right!

definitions.text: Thus diminutive female indicated she's all right!

parts.words: Thus diminutive female indicated she's all right
parts.note: a small woman being a 'bit of all right' leads to the slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: A petite woman reassuring everyone that she is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang: 'a bit of all right' is an attractive person, and this phrase is similar slang for a pretty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for an attractive young woman, seen as frivolous.

clue.text: Stock food over a long period of time

parts.note: over a week means for a week
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: Supplies of food kept over a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder for livestock such as cattle and horses is stock food.

clue.text: Understand body is so far down?

definitions.meaning: a measure of depth of six feet, as deep as a body is buried

explanation.surface: Someone puzzling over how deep a buried body lies.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a puzzle is to understand it; the unit of six feet measures depth, roughly a grave's.

clue.text: Injure tax-man

parts.note: scat is an old word for a tax or tribute
he is a man

explanation.surface: A demand to hurt the tax collector.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm or wound someone is to injure them; the word survives mostly in unscathed.

clue.text: Spanish senor's requirement for middle name?

definitions.text: Spanish senor's requirement for middle name?

parts.words: Spanish senor's requirement for middle name
parts.note: the Spanish word for sir needs a mark over its middle letter n, which is missing here

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman needing a middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle name' is the middle letter N of senor, which in Spanish carries a wavy mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy accent written over the n in Spanish words like señor.

clue.text: On return, swimmer's opening port

indicators.note: on its return the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: a ray is a swimmer, a fish; the 's means 'is'
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: A swimmer coming back to an opening harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Yarmouth is a port on the Norfolk coast of England; there is also a Yarmouth on the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Without students having broken record, sign domestic summons?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the star sign goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the bull, Taurus, is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: the students break into the record, sitting inside it

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
L is a learner or student, so two students are LL

explanation.surface: Without students breaking the record, a sign of the landlord's summons to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside, not lacking; 'having broken' means the learners split the record open.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord pulled to ring a bell and call a servant, once a household summons.

clue.text: Element at the heart of score-draw

indicators.note: only the central letters of the scoreline are wanted, the outer ones going

parts.note: a one-one result is a score draw on the football pools

explanation.surface: A key factor at the centre of a drawn football match.
explanation.walkthrough: On British football pools a score draw is a drawn match with goals, like 1-1; its middle letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas in group 18, atomic number 10, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Angry German, getting covered, turned off hose?

indicators.note: the German is covered by, placed inside, the other set of letters
off, as in gone wrong, means the letters of turned are rearranged
angry, worked up, means the letters of German are stirred

explanation.surface: A furious German, covered up, switching off a hosepipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams, 'off' and 'Angry', one sitting inside the other per 'getting covered'. 'hose' means stockings, not a garden pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose in the sense of stockings or tights is worn beneath outer clothes.
